item.content:encoded:
Love it, but two small issues:

One: I came into this having absolutely zero idea what "synesthesia" meant, so most of this article was lost on me until I read the discussion and managed to put everything together. Maybe there's something that can be done about that, maybe not, but it was a bit annoying.

Two: As soon as the label "SCP-979-V1" was mentioned, the description of what happens to people affected by this thing started describing the symptoms in a past-tense third-person-singular tone - that is, as if it was recounting the details of a specific case, rather than explaining what this thing does to all people. It read more like a test log than a description, and that kind of threw me off. Tonal edit, please?

+1

item.content:encoded: Well you see, the SCP causes synesthesia of all senses. You could, but it causes such sensory overload that you can't sleep, and start hallucinating, mental changes, eventually sensory overload and shut down. So while you're feeling a smell you also see, hear, taste the smell, then you can feel, smell, hear, and taste what you see, and it just domino effects from there. All other senses are bouncing right off each other.
